mainTopic: Proving a כתובה of two hundred through witnesses to virgin-wedding customs, guarding against double collection, and explaining those wedding customs
overview: This amud first finishes רבינא's answer to why we do not simply assume the bride was a virgin, as most brides are. He changes 'every virgin's wedding is talked about' to 'most are', so the missing publicity only weakens the majority, and witnesses can still decide the case. The גמרא then asks about the משנה's witnesses to the הינומא: could she collect with witnesses and later collect again with her כתובה document? רבי אבהו says a שובר (receipt) is written. רב פפא says the משנה is about a place where no כתובה document is written. A second version puts this debate on a ברייתא about a lost, hidden or burned כתובה. That forces a new reading: a woman who says she lost it is treated like one who hid it, and she is paid only if witnesses say it burned. The גמרא adds that where there is no other protection, everyone agrees a שובר is written. It then explains two virgin-wedding customs: the cup of תרומה wine, which shows she is 'first', and the sealed or open barrel of wine. Finally, a new ברייתא begins asking what is said while dancing before the כלה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רבינא's first answer: this woman had no publicity
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's first answer ends: since this woman's wedding created no publicity, the majority is weakened in her case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this woman, since her wedding had no publicity, the majority is weakened for her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רבינא's answer to the question 'Why not just follow the majority?' He says the lack of publicity at her wedding weakens the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we would assume she was a virgin, because most brides are. But a virgin's wedding is usually talked about, and nobody talked about hers. That missing publicity weakens the majority, so we cannot simply rely on it here.

keyTerms.meaning: Publicity; people talking about the wedding
The majority (here: most brides are virgins)

phrases.english: And this one, since she has no publicity —
the majority is weakened for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a factor (no publicity) that weakens the majority
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not automatically follow the majority, because her wedding lacked the publicity a virgin's wedding usually has

steps.title: If every virgin's wedding is talked about, her witnesses must be lying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the wording 'every virgin bride has publicity': if that is always true, witnesses who say she was a virgin bride would have to be false.
steps.simpleTranslation: If every woman who marries as a virgin has publicity, then when witnesses come, what good are they? These are lying witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's wording. If every virgin's wedding is talked about, then her silent wedding proves she was not a virgin, and the witnesses could not be believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says witnesses who saw her go out with a הינומא win her two hundred. But if publicity always happens at a virgin's wedding, the lack of it is total proof against her. Then the witnesses would be contradicting a sure fact. So the word 'every' (כל) cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Every woman who marries as a virgin
What of it? What difference does it make?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the witnesses really are liars. It is showing that the word 'every' leads to a result that clashes with the משנה, so the wording must be changed.

phrases.aramaic: אִי כׇּל הַנִּשֵּׂאת בְּתוּלָה יֵשׁ לָהּ קוֹל —
phrases.english: If every woman who marries as a virgin has publicity —
when witnesses come, what of it?
These are lying witnesses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כׇּל הַנִּשֵּׂאת בְּתוּלָה יֵשׁ לָהּ קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבינא's answer in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If publicity always comes with a virgin's wedding, then no publicity is total proof, and the משנה's witnesses could never be believed

steps.title: רבינא changes 'every' to 'most'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא restates his idea: most virgin brides have publicity, and the lack of it only weakens the majority, so witnesses can still win.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: most women who marry as virgins have publicity. And this woman, since she has no publicity, the majority is weakened for her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא fixes his wording. Publicity is only usual, not guaranteed, so its absence weakens the majority without proving anything for certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two majorities that cancel each other out: most brides are virgins, but most virgin brides have publicity. Since neither side is sure, witnesses who saw the הינומא can decide the case in her favor. This fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier version is dropped

steps.whatToRemember: Lack of publicity weakens the 'most brides are virgins' majority, but it does not prove anything. So witnesses to virgin-wedding customs can still prove she gets two hundred.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב הַנִּשֵּׂאת בְּתוּלָה יֵשׁ לָהּ קוֹל,
phrases.english: most women who marry as virgins have publicity,
and this one, since she has no publicity —
the majority is weakened for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by changing one word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Publicity always comes with a virgin's wedding
steps.terutzMaskana: Publicity usually comes with a virgin's wedding, so its absence only weakens the majority and witnesses can still decide the case

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about witnesses and the הינומא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line: if there are witnesses that she went out with a הינומא, her כתובה is two hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are witnesses that she went out with a הינומא, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה to set up a new question about it. The question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that she collects two hundred based on witnesses alone, without showing a כתובה document. That detail is what the next question will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: A special veil or canopy that virgin brides traditionally wore when leaving their father's house
Etc.; the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁיָּצְתָה בְּהִינוּמָא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she went out with a hinnuma, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' covers the rest of the משנה: or with her hair loose, and then her כתובה is two hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses to virgin-wedding customs entitle her to a כתובה of two hundred

steps.title: Could she collect twice, once with witnesses and once with the document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא worries she might collect with witnesses in one court and then collect again with her כתובה document in another court.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that she may bring witnesses in this court and collect, and then bring out her כתובה in that court and collect with it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the משנה's ruling: collecting without the document opens the door to collecting twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman hands over her כתובה document when she gets paid, so she cannot use it again. Here she is paid through witnesses and keeps the document. So what stops her from showing it in a different court and getting paid a second time?

keyTerms.meaning: She brings out or produces (witnesses or a document)

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps she brings out witnesses
in this court, and collects,
and then brings out her ketubah
in that court, and collects with it?
phrases.notes: The same word 'האי' is used both times, but here it means a different court from the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she collects based on witnesses without a document
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since she keeps the document, she could use it later in another court and get paid twice

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the husband gets a receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns from the משנה that the husband is given a receipt (שובר), which protects him from a second claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: This shows that we write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the worry. Since the משנה lets her collect with witnesses, it must be that a receipt is written for the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she ever comes back with the כתובה document, the husband shows the receipt and proves he already paid. The phrase 'זאת אומרת' means he is drawing this rule out of the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows; we learn from here
We write a receipt confirming payment

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to a larger question in the laws of debts: whether a debtor who pays can protect himself with a receipt, or whether the lender must hand back the document.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
This shows that we write a receipt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical safeguard learned from the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband gets a שובר, so a second claim with the document can be blocked

steps.title: רב פפא: the משנה is in a place with no כתובה documents
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers differently: the משנה is talking about a place where no כתובה document is written, so there is nothing to collect with twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We are dealing with a place where they do not write a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another answer to the same worry. In the משנה's case there is no document at all, so a second collection is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not need a receipt. He limits the משנה to a place where the כתובה is owed by law without a written document. In that case witnesses are the only way to prove the amount, and the double-collection fear never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where they do not write (a document)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We are dealing with a place where they do not write a ketubah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 5, different from רבי אבהו's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is set where no כתובה document exists, so she cannot collect twice
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the double-collection worry: רבי אבהו says the husband gets a receipt; רב פפא says the משנה is about a place with no כתובה document.

steps.title: Another version: the same discussion is placed on a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some place the רבי אבהו / רב פפא discussion on a ברייתא instead. That ברייתא lists cases where her document is lost, hidden, or burned, along with more virgin-wedding customs, and says witnesses to any of them give her two hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on a ברייתא: If her כתובה was lost, or she hid her כתובה, or her כתובה was burned; if they danced before her, played before her, passed before her a cup of good news, or a cloth of virginity. If she has witnesses to any one of these, her כתובה is two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of where the discussion belongs. In this version it is attached to a ברייתא, not to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks of a woman whose document is missing (lost, hidden, or burned) and who proves her virgin status through witnesses to wedding customs. The same worry applies: what if the 'missing' document shows up later? According to this version, רבי אבהו and רב פפא were answering that worry about this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (on a different source)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
A cup of good news, a wedding custom for virgins
A cloth of virginity, another virgin-wedding custom

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not repeat the question and the two answers here. It means the same worry and the same two answers are now attached to this ברייתא instead of the משנה.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on a baraita:
phrases.notes: 'It' means the whole question with the answers of רבי אבהו and רב פפא.

phrases.english: If she lost her ketubah, if she hid her ketubah,
phrases.notes: 'Hid' means she put it away and says she cannot find it.

phrases.english: if her ketubah was burned,
if they danced before her, if they played before her,
if they passed before her a cup of good tidings,
or a cloth of virginity.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בְּאֶחָד מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ —
phrases.english: If she has witnesses to any one of all these —
her ketubah is two hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the discussion of steps 5 to 7 onto a ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When her כתובה document is missing, witnesses to any virgin-wedding custom entitle her to a כתובה of two hundred

steps.title: The double-collection worry, now aimed at the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the same worry as before, this time on the ברייתא: she might collect twice, once with witnesses and once with her document.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should worry: maybe she brings witnesses to one court and collects, then brings her כתובה document to another court and collects again with it!
steps.whatsHappening: In this second version, the גמרא repeats its worry about the ברייתא. If witnesses alone can get her paid, she might also use her document somewhere else and get paid twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets her collect two hundred based on witnesses alone. But a written כתובה could still exist and be used in a different court. The worry is double payment on one debt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be worried about it

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like an exact repeat of step 5. It is the same question, but in this version the גמרא is asking it about the ברייתא, not the משנה. That difference matters later.

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps she produces witnesses
in this court and collects,
and then produces her כתובה document
in that court and collects with it!
phrases.notes: The same word בהאי is used both times, but here it means a different, second court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following step 8, the גמרא now runs the same question on the ברייתא instead of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that witnesses alone get her two hundred
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying her on witnesses alone leaves her document free to be used again, so she could collect twice.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a receipt is written
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says this shows that a receipt (שובר) is written for the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: This shows that we write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives the same answer as before. Because the ברייתא lets her collect with witnesses, we know the husband gets a receipt, so he is protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she later shows up with her document, the husband shows the receipt proving he already paid. The ברייתא's ruling teaches that receipts are written.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt proving a debt was paid

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:
This shows that one writes a receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת כּוֹתְבִין שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning a practice (writing a receipt) from the ruling itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying on witnesses leaves the husband open to a second claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: A receipt is written, so a second claim can be blocked.

steps.title: רב פפא: a place where no כתובה is written
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ruling is about a place where no כתובה document is written at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We are dealing with a place where people do not write a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer. If no document exists, there is nothing she could use to collect a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the worry instead of solving it with a receipt. In this version, though, he is saying it about the ברייתא, and that sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
We are dealing with a place where they do not write a כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רבי אבהו to the same worry.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A written כתובה might exist and be used again.
steps.terutzMaskana: No document is written there, so there is no risk of double collection.

steps.title: But the ברייתא speaks of a lost כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the ברייתא talks about a woman who lost her כתובה, so a document clearly existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches 'she lost her כתובה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא. You can only lose a document you had, so the ברייתא can't be about a place with no documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer fit the משנה well. But the ברייתא lists cases of a lost, hidden, or burned כתובה, and each of those assumes a written document.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (pointing to words in the source)

phrases.english: But it teaches: "She lost her כתובה"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the ברייתא is about a place with no written כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own wording, 'she lost her כתובה', shows a document existed.

steps.title: He wrote her one anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in this case the husband wrote her a כתובה even though the local custom is not to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he himself wrote one for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. The place doesn't usually write a כתובה, but this particular husband did, and she lost it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the 'no-document place' setting while explaining how she could have a document to lose. It was a private choice by the husband, not the local custom.

phrases.english: Where he himself wrote one for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lost כתובה means this can't be a no-document place.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a no-document place, but this husband wrote one anyway.

steps.title: Then the worry returns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if a document exists, the old danger is back. She might find it and collect again.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, she will bring it out and collect with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the fix brings back the original problem. If there is a document, it could turn up later and be used for a second payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's whole point was that no document exists. Once we say the husband wrote one, the risk of double collection is back.

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף מַפְּקָא לַהּ וְגָבְיָא בַּהּ!
phrases.english: In the end, she will bring it out and collect with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף מַפְּקָא לַהּ וְגָבְיָא בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husband wrote a כתובה himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any existing document can be produced later, so the double-collection worry returns.

steps.title: 'Lost' means lost in a fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'lost' in the ברייתא means destroyed in a fire, so the document no longer exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'lost' mean? Lost in the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'lost' to mean the document burned up. If it is gone for good, she can't produce it later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the danger again. A burned document can never be brought to another court.

phrases.english: What does "she lost" mean?
She lost it in the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lost' means the document still exists somewhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Lost' means burned, so it can't come back.

steps.title: Three problems with the 'fire' reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises three problems. 'Burned' is already listed. The 'hidden' case still has the risk. And there would be no reason to list 'lost' at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as 'burned'! And also, what can you say about 'hid it'? And further, why do I need 'lost' at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the 'lost in a fire' answer with three separate problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the ברייתא already lists 'burned' as its own case, so 'lost' can't mean the same thing. Second, a hidden document still exists, so the double-collection worry stays for that case. Third, if 'lost' just means 'burned', listing it adds nothing.

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as "it was burned"!
And furthermore: "she hid it", what is there to say?
And further: why do I need "she lost it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes 'lost' the same as 'burned' and adds nothing new. It also leaves the 'hidden' case open to double collection.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא a new way: 'lost' is like 'hidden'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. Any 'lost' claim is treated like hiding the document in front of us, and she is paid only if witnesses say it was burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: any 'lost' case is like she hid it in front of us, and we do not pay her until witnesses say her כתובה was burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier fixes and reads the ברייתא differently. A woman who says she lost her כתובה is treated as if she might still have it, so she is paid only when witnesses say it burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I lost it' doesn't prove the document is gone, so it's like she is hiding it. Only testimony that it burned removes the risk of a second payment. That is how the ברייתא is now understood.

phrases.english: Rather: any case of "she lost it"
is like she hid it in front of us,
and we do not give her payment
until witnesses say her כתובה was burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כֹּל אִיבְּדָה כִּי הִטְמִינָה בְּפָנֵינוּ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16 knocks down the earlier fixes, this gives a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lost', 'hidden', and 'burned' are three separate cases that each pay on witnesses alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Lost' is treated like 'hidden'. She is paid only when witnesses say the document burned.

steps.title: Which version applies where
steps.stepSummary: Whoever applies the discussion to the ברייתא would surely apply it to the משנה. But whoever applies it to the משנה would not apply it to the ברייתא, because of the difficulty raised.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it on the ברייתא, all the more so on the משנה. The one who teaches it on the משנה, but not on the ברייתא, because of the difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes by comparing the two versions from step 8. It explains how each version relates to the other source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has no talk of a lost document, so רב פפא's answer fits it easily. That is why the ברייתא version surely covers the משנה too. The ברייתא, though, mentions a lost כתובה, which makes רב פפא's answer hard, so the משנה version would not extend to the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches it (applies it to)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the רבי אבהו / רב פפא debate. On the משנה, both answers work smoothly. On the ברייתא, רב פפא's answer runs into the 'lost כתובה' problem, which forces a new reading of the ברייתא. So the ברייתא version covers the משנה too, but not the reverse.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the ברייתא
all the more so on the משנה.
But the one who teaches it on the משנה
but not on the ברייתא, because of the difficulty.
phrases.notes: The difficulty is the 'she lost her כתובה' problem from step 12, which shows the ברייתא is about a place where documents exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַבָּרַיְיתָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַמַּתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the second version and compares it to the first.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The debate fits the משנה in both versions. Applying it to the ברייתא is harder because the ברייתא speaks of a lost כתובה.

steps.title: Could she collect twice using הינומא witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'if there are witnesses' and worries she could bring the same witnesses to two courts and collect twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding 'if there are witnesses': let us worry that she brings witnesses of the הינומא to this court and collects, and then brings them to another court and collects again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case, where witnesses saw her go out with a הינומא. It asks whether she could use these witnesses to collect her כתובה twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses are not a document that gets torn up after payment. So nothing seems to stop her from showing the same proof in a second בית דין and getting paid again. This is the same 'double collection' worry from the earlier steps, now aimed at witnesses instead of a document.

keyTerms.meaning: A special veil or canopy a בתולה bride was carried in

phrases.english: 'If there are witnesses,' etc.
But let us worry that perhaps she will produce

phrases.aramaic: עֵדֵי הִינּוּמָא בְּהַאי בֵּית דִּין וְגָבְיָא,
phrases.english: witnesses of the hinnuma in this court and collect,
and then again produce witnesses of the hinnuma
in another court and collect!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the double-collection worry from the document discussion to the משנה's witness case
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that הינומא witnesses are enough for her to collect two hundred
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses can be reused in another court, so she might collect twice

steps.title: Where there is no other way, we write a receipt
steps.stepSummary: When there is no other protection, everyone agrees the husband gets a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where it is not possible otherwise, we certainly write a receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in this case the husband gets a שובר, a written receipt, proving he already paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was a debate about whether we write a שובר. The answer here is that even the side that usually avoids writing one agrees when there is no other way to protect the husband. Here nothing can be torn up, so a שובר is the only protection.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt showing a debt was paid

steps.whatToRemember: Even if we normally avoid writing a שובר, we write one when there is no other way to stop a second collection.

phrases.english: In a place where it is not possible
phrases.notes: He means there is no other way to protect the husband, since there is no כתובה document to tear up.

phrases.english: we certainly write a receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמָקוֹם דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר וַדַּאי כָּתְבִינַן שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the double-collection challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the 'no receipt' view to cases where another protection exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since some hold we never write a שובר, she might collect twice
steps.terutzMaskana: Where there is no alternative, everyone agrees a שובר is written

steps.title: What is the 'cup of good tidings'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's sign of a בתולה and asks what the cup means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They passed before her a cup of good tidings.' What is a 'cup of good tidings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another sign from the ברייתא that the bride was a בתולה, and asks what this cup was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word. The גמרא wants to know what the custom was and why it shows she was a בתולה. This sets up the answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of good tidings (a wedding custom)

phrases.english: 'They passed before her a cup of good tidings.'
What is a 'cup of good tidings'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new detail in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and purpose of the 'cup of good tidings'

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: a cup of תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says it is a cup of תרומה wine, showing she could have eaten תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: They pass a cup of תרומה wine before her, meaning: this woman was fit to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the cup held תרומה wine. It hinted that she would have been allowed to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the cup shows she was fit to marry a כהן and eat תרומה. רב אדא בר אהבה sees this as a sign of her being a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ.
phrases.english: They pass a cup of terumah wine before her.
Meaning: this woman would have been fit
to eat terumah.
phrases.notes: He means if she had married a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: כּוֹס יַיִן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the cup
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A cup of תרומה wine, showing she was fit to eat תרומה

steps.title: רב פפא: an אלמנה can also eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that an אלמנה married to a כהן also eats תרומה, so this proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged it: Is that to say a widow does not eat תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation. A widow may also marry a regular כהן and eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cup only means 'fit to eat תרומה,' it does not set a בתולה apart. A widow fits that too, so the sign proves nothing about being a בתולה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ אַלְמָנָה מִי לָא אָכְלָה בִּתְרוּמָה?
phrases.english: Is that to say a widow does not eat terumah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's reading that the cup shows she was fit to eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow can also eat תרומה, so the sign does not single out a בתולה

steps.title: רב פפא: she is 'first,' like תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the cup means she is 'first,' just as תרומה is the first portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: This one is 'first,' just as תרומה is 'first.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own explanation of the cup. תרומה is called 'first,' and the bride is 'first' because no man has been with her yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is no longer about being fit to eat תרומה. It is about being 'first,' like תרומה. This fits only a בתולה, so רב פפא's own question no longer applies.
steps.whatToRemember: The cup of תרומה wine hints that the bride is 'first,' like תרומה, and not just that she may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
This one is 'first,' just as terumah is 'first.'
phrases.notes: תרומה is called 'first' because it is the first portion taken from the crop. The bride is 'first' because she is a בתולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זוֹ רֵאשִׁית, כִּתְרוּמָה רֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cup shows she was fit to eat תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: The cup shows she is 'first,' like תרומה, which fits only a בתולה

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a barrel of wine is passed before her
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: the custom was to pass a barrel of wine before the bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: They pass a barrel of wine before her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another wedding custom from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says a barrel of wine was passed before the bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different custom from the cup. The next step explains how the barrel shows whether she was a בתולה.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They pass a barrel of wine before her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second wedding custom
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A barrel of wine is passed before the bride

steps.title: Sealed barrel for a virgin, open barrel for a non-virgin
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains: a sealed barrel is passed before a בתולה and an open one before a בעולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: For a בתולה they pass a sealed barrel before her. For a בעולה they pass an open barrel before her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains רבי יהודה's custom. Whether the barrel is sealed or open shows whether the bride is a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed barrel stands for a woman who has not been with a man, and an open one for a woman who has. So the custom is used both for a בתולה and for a בעולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not a virgin

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
For a virgin, they pass a sealed one before her,
for a non-virgin, they pass an open one before her.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוּלָה מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ סְתוּמָה, בְּעוּלָה מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ פְּתוּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יהודה's barrel works
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sealed barrel for a בתולה, open barrel for a בעולה

steps.title: Why pass any barrel before a non-virgin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a בעולה needs an open barrel at all. Just pass nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let them pass one before a בתולה, and before a בעולה not pass anything at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב אדא בר אהבה's rule. Not giving a barrel would already show she is a בעולה, so why give her an open one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sealed barrel marks a בתולה, then having no barrel should mark a בעולה. Making a public sign for the בעולה seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Why? Let them pass one before a virgin,
and before a non-virgin not pass anything at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? נִיעַבַּר קַמֵּי בְּתוּלָה וְקַמֵּי בְּעוּלָה לָא נִיעַבַּר כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the open-barrel part of רב אדא בר אהבה's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for an open barrel for a בעולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No barrel at all would already show she is a בעולה

steps.title: The open barrel stops a false claim
steps.stepSummary: Without a clear sign, a בעולה could grab two hundred and claim the barrel was skipped by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes she may seize two hundred and say: 'I was a בתולה, and the fact that they did not pass one before me was just because something got in their way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the open barrel is needed. If nothing is passed, she could later claim the sealed barrel was simply missed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no barrel can be explained away as an accident. An open barrel is a clear sign people will remember, so she cannot claim two hundred as a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: She seized (took the money on her own)
Two hundred (the כתובה of a בתולה)
Being prevented by circumstances beyond their control

steps.whatToRemember: A clear sign, the open barrel, is better than no sign, because no sign can be explained away as an accident.

phrases.english: Sometimes she may seize two hundred,
and say: I was a virgin,
and the fact that they did not pass one before me,
was just because something beyond their control stopped them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why an open barrel is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No barrel is enough to show she is a בעולה
steps.terutzMaskana: An open barrel is needed so she cannot claim the sealed barrel was missed by accident

steps.title: How do we dance before the bride?
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens: what does one say while dancing before the כלה? בית שמאי begin to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How does one dance before the כלה? בית שמאי say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about what to say while dancing at a wedding. This line is a setup: בית שמאי's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic: the praises said to the bride. The question is set up here, and the opinions of בית שמאי and בית הלל continue past this point.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How does one dance before the bride?
phrases.notes: He means what words do we say about her while dancing.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד מְרַקְּדִין לִפְנֵי הַכַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to wedding customs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the question of what is said when dancing before the כלה
